The TARGET consists of three definitions:

1. Def7: Given an arithmetic theory F (a set of arithmetic sentences) under the hypothesis that F is recursively enumerable (F.RE), Def7 F is (noncomputably) defined to be the arithmetic sentence F.craig.consistent.val—that is, the sentence ¬Prov_{F.craig}(⌜⊥⌝), where F.craig is the Δ₁-presented axiom set with the same theorems as F obtained by Craig's trick, and Prov_{F.craig} is the standard provability predicate built from that Δ₁ presentation. No further hypotheses on F (such as consistency or containing 𝗜𝚺₁) are required.

2. Def8: Given a set of arithmetic sentences K (of type Def1) and an arithmetic theory F under the hypothesis that F is recursively enumerable (F.RE), Def8 K F is the proposition that both (a) Def5 K F holds, i.e., K equals F.theory (the set of all arithmetic sentences derivable from F in classical first-order logic), and (b) Def7 F ∈ K, i.e., the consistency sentence F.craig.consistent.val (¬Prov_{F.craig}(⌜⊥⌝)) is an element of K. No other conditions on K or F (such as consistency, truth in the standard model, or arithmetic strength) are required.

3. Def9: Given a set of arithmetic sentences K (of type Def1) and an arithmetic theory F under the hypothesis that F is recursively enumerable (F.RE), Def9 K F is the proposition that F.craig.localReflectionOn Set.univ ⊆ K—that is, for every arithmetic sentence σ, the sentence Prov_{F.craig}(⌜σ⌝) 🡒 σ (where Prov_{F.craig} is the standard provability predicate built from the Δ₁ presentation F.craig of F) is an element of K. Notably, unlike Def8, Def9 does not require Def5 K F (it does not require K = F.theory or any other relation between K and F.theory), nor does it require K to be deductively closed, consistent, or true in the standard model.

divergences.description: Def7, Def8, and Def9 model F extensionally as a recursively enumerable set of arithmetic sentences and form provability and consistency using F.craig, which noncomputably picks an arbitrary Δ₁ presentation of F's theorems. Because Con(F) and local reflection are intensional—different Δ₁ presentations of the same RE theory can have inequivalent consistency sentences and different local reflection sets—this suppresses presentation-dependence compared to a fixed machine specification F_e ([P-K359]) or a given syntactic representation of F ([P-K345], [P-K354]).

In Def9, F(⌜φ⌝) is restricted to the standard provability predicate Prov_{F.craig}(⌜φ⌝) of an RE arithmetic theory F, with φ ranging over ℒₒᵣ sentences. While this matches Koellner's informal pointwise scheme for a formal system F over L_PA in [P-K354], it is narrower than Reinhardt's Theorem 3 in [P-K354], where F(x) is an arbitrary one-variable formula (not necessarily an RE provability predicate and potentially containing K) and φ ranges over all sentences of the epistemic theory S.

Relative to [P-K359], which refers to knowing that the machine F_e 'works correctly' (soundness, K(F_e ⊆ T)), Def8 pairs K = F.theory with the strictly weaker consistency condition Con(F) ∈ K. This accurately matches the author's claim (ii)—with soundness handled separately via local reflection in Def9—but weakens the correctness condition in [P-K359].

judgement.summary: The three definitions accurately implement the author's claims (i)–(iii) under the declared set-membership stand-in for K, with minor caveats concerning the arbitrary Craig-trick Δ₁ presentation of F, the restriction of Def9's predicate to Prov_{F.craig} over ℒₒᵣ rather than an arbitrary formula F(x), and Def8's use of consistency rather than [P-K359]'s soundness condition.
